In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence that NAD(+) is bound to the enzyme in any other way than by the two pyrophosphate oxygen atoms.
the NAD(+) sulphite adduct is not a suitable model for the ternary enzyme complexes.
the NAD-sulfite complex does not bind to either enzyme, and the rate of binding of NAD to either enzyme does not depend on the conformation of the enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the binding of NAD(++) to lactate dehyrogenase and malate deshydrogenase does not appear to involve a major conformational change in the enzyme.
the NAD-sulfite adduct binds to both lactate dehydroganse and malate dehyrogenase in a similar way to NAD(+) itself.
